components.note: 广 (a roof on a wall) — buildings and rooms: 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store, 度. Here also the simplified form of 廣, broad.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 每天早上都有人在广场上跳舞。
example.pinyin: měitiān zǎoshang dōu yǒu rén zài guǎngchǎng shàng tiàowǔ.
example.english: Every morning there are people dancing in the square.
example.fact: St. Peter's Square in Vatican City was designed by the sculptor and architect Gian Lorenzo Bernini in the 17th century, with its elliptical colonnade of 284 columns arranged to symbolically embrace visitors like outstretched arms. The square can hold around 300,000 people during major papal events. Its central obelisk was originally brought from Egypt by the Roman Emperor Caligula in 37 AD.

examples.hanzi: 广场上有很多孩子在放风筝。
examples.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō háizi zài fàng fēngzheng.
examples.english: Many children are flying kites in the square.

examples.hanzi: 我们在市中心的广场见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shì zhōngxīn de guǎngchǎng jiànmiàn ba.
examples.english: Let's meet at the plaza in the city center.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and listening: 听, 闻, 聋; 职 is the duty one hears and remembers.
只 (zhī) is a near sound match for zhí; also in 织 zhī and 识 shí.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 他终于得到了梦想的职位。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú dédào le mèngxiǎng de zhíwèi.
example.english: He finally got his dream position.
example.fact: China's imperial examination system, established during the Sui Dynasty around 605 AD, tested candidates for government positions and lasted for roughly 1,300 years until it was abolished in 1905. Candidates could spend decades preparing and retaking the exams, and passing could elevate a commoner into the ruling class. This meritocratic model later influenced the design of civil service systems in Britain and the United States in the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 这个职位需要两年工作经验。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhíwèi xūyào liǎng nián gōngzuò jīngyàn.
examples.english: This position requires two years of work experience.

examples.hanzi: 他想申请公司的管理职位。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng shēnqǐng gōngsī de guǎnlǐ zhíwèi.
examples.english: He wants to apply for a management position at the company.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 这种植物被称为“沙漠之王”。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng zhíwù bèi chēngwéi “shāmò zhī wáng”.
example.english: This plant is called the "king of the desert."
example.fact: Welwitschia mirabilis, a strange desert plant native to Namibia and Angola, is sometimes called a "living fossil" because individual plants can live for well over 1,000 years, with some estimated at nearly 2,000 years old. It survives in one of the driest deserts on Earth by absorbing moisture from coastal fog through its leaves. Despite its resilience, it produces only two leaves in its entire lifetime, which simply keep growing and splitting.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市被称为“东方明珠”。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì bèi chēngwéi "Dōngfāng Míngzhū".
examples.english: This city is called the "Pearl of the Orient."

examples.hanzi: 人们把他称为“活字典”。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen bǎ tā chēngwéi "huó zìdiǎn".
examples.english: People call him a "walking dictionary."

components.note: 黄 (huáng) — yellow; as a part it sounds out 簧 huáng and 磺 huáng.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 秋天的时候，很多叶子都变成了黄色。
example.pinyin: qiūtiān de shíhou, hěn duō yèzi dōu biànchéng le huángsè.
example.english: In autumn, many leaves turn yellow.
example.fact: Autumn leaves turn yellow because chlorophyll, the green pigment used for photosynthesis, breaks down as days shorten and temperatures drop, revealing yellow and orange carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but masked by the dominant green. These carotenoids are the same class of pigments that give carrots their color. Red pigments, by contrast, are often newly produced in autumn rather than simply unmasked.

examples.hanzi: 他穿了一件黄色的外套。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn huángsè de wàitào.
examples.english: He wore a yellow coat.

examples.hanzi: 红灯变成黄色时，要慢慢停车。
examples.pinyin: Hóngdēng biàn chéng huángsè shí, yào mànman tíngchē.
examples.english: When the light turns yellow, you need to slow down and stop.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.

example.hanzi: 这种欺骗行为真是可恶。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng qīpiàn xíngwéi zhēnshi kěwù.
example.english: This kind of deceptive behavior is truly repulsive.
example.fact: The blobfish, often voted the world's "ugliest animal," only looks gelatinous and repulsive when removed from the deep-sea pressure it normally lives under, at depths of 600 to 1,200 meters off the coast of Australia. In its natural habitat, the pressure keeps its body properly shaped, and it actually looks like an ordinary fish. It won the title of world's ugliest animal in a 2013 poll by the Ugly Animal Preservation Society, intended to raise awareness for unglamorous endangered species.

examples.hanzi: 他竟然骗老人的钱，真可恶！
examples.pinyin: Tā jìngrán piàn lǎorén de qián, zhēn kěwù!
examples.english: He actually cheated an old person out of money, how despicable!

examples.hanzi: 这只蚊子太可恶了，一晚上没让我睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī wénzi tài kěwù le, yì wǎnshang méi ràng wǒ shuìjiào.
examples.english: This mosquito is so annoying; it kept me up all night.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 今晚的星星特别明亮。
example.pinyin: jīnwǎn de xīngxing tèbié míngliàng.
example.english: Tonight's stars are especially bright.
example.fact: The light from most stars visible to the naked eye left those stars years, centuries, or even millennia ago, meaning we are essentially looking into the past every time we look up at the night sky. The nearest star system to our sun, Alpha Centauri, is about 4.37 light-years away, so its light takes over four years to reach Earth. Some stars we see may have already died by the time their light finally arrives.

examples.hanzi: 晚上能看到很多星星。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang néng kàn dào hěn duō xīngxing.
examples.english: You can see lots of stars at night.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们数着天上的星星。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen shǔ zhe tiān shàng de xīngxing.
examples.english: The children are counting the stars in the sky.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.hanzi: 这本书一共有一百页。
example.pinyin: zhè běn shū yígòng yǒu yìbǎi yè.
example.english: This book has one hundred pages in total.
example.fact: The abacus, one of the earliest calculating tools, was used in ancient China, Rome, and Mesopotamia to perform arithmetic including counting in the hundreds, long before written positional number systems became widespread. Skilled abacus users in East Asia can still outperform calculators for certain addition and subtraction tasks through a technique called "anzan," mental abacus calculation. Some Japanese schools continue to teach abacus use specifically to strengthen mental math ability.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服一百块钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yì bǎi kuài qián.
examples.english: This piece of clothing costs one hundred yuan.

examples.hanzi: 我们班有一百个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu yì bǎi ge xuésheng.
examples.english: There are one hundred students in our class.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 踏 is stepping on or treading.
沓 (tà) — close sound: 踏 tà. 沓 also sounds out 蹋 tà.

example.hanzi: 他一脚踏进了水里。
example.pinyin: Tā yì jiǎo tà jìn le shuǐ lǐ.
example.english: He stepped right into the water.
example.fact: 踏 is the written word for stepping; speech prefers 踩. It forms 踏青 ('tread the green', a spring outing) and 踏实, read tāshi, meaning 'steady' or 'at ease' (a special reading).

examples.hanzi: 他踏上了回家的火车。
examples.pinyin: Tā tà shàng le huíjiā de huǒchē.
examples.english: He stepped onto the train home.

examples.hanzi: 请不要踏草坪。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào tà cǎopíng.
examples.english: Please don't walk on the lawn.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.

example.hanzi: 他没有给出确切的答案。
example.pinyin: tā méiyǒu gěi chū quèqiè de dá'àn.
example.english: He didn't give a definite answer.
example.fact: The value of pi has been calculated to over 100 trillion digits using modern supercomputers, even though only about 40 digits are needed for any practical engineering calculation, including plotting a spacecraft's trajectory to the edge of the observable universe with atomic-level precision. Ancient Babylonian mathematicians approximated pi as 3.125 nearly 4,000 years ago. The pursuit of ever more exact digits today is mostly a way to stress-test computing hardware.

examples.hanzi: 请告诉我确切的时间。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ quèqiè de shíjiān.
examples.english: Please tell me the exact time.

examples.hanzi: 没有人知道确切的原因。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén zhīdào quèqiè de yuányīn.
examples.english: No one knows the exact reason.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 援 is to lend a hand.
爰 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 援 yuán, also in 暖 nuǎn and 缓 huǎn.

example.hanzi: 各地纷纷派出医疗队支援灾区。
example.pinyin: gèdì fēnfēn pàichū yīliáoduì zhīyuán zāiqū.
example.english: Regions everywhere sent medical teams to support the disaster area.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, launched by the United States in 1948, provided about $13 billion (equivalent to well over $150 billion today) in economic support to help rebuild sixteen war-torn Western European countries after World War II. The aid helped rebuild infrastructure, stabilize currencies, and is widely credited with helping prevent the spread of communism in Western Europe during the early Cold War. Secretary of State George Marshall received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1953 for the initiative.

examples.hanzi: 其他城市也来支援我们。
examples.pinyin: Qítā chéngshì yě lái zhīyuán wǒmen.
examples.english: Other cities also came to support us.

examples.hanzi: 志愿者们赶来支援灾区。
examples.pinyin: Zhìyuànzhěmen gǎn lái zhīyuán zāiqū.
examples.english: Volunteers rushed to help the disaster area.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and boundaries, as in 院, 陆, 阶; 限 is a limit.
艮 (gèn) is only a loose hint for xiàn; 根 gēn and 跟 gēn share it.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.

example.hanzi: 医生限制他每天摄入的糖分。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiànzhì tā měitiān shèrù de tángfèn.
example.english: The doctor restricts his daily sugar intake.
example.fact: The world's first speed limit, imposed by the UK's Locomotive Act of 1865, capped "horseless carriages" at 4 mph in the country and required a person to walk ahead waving a red flag to warn pedestrians. This "Red Flag Act" was eventually repealed in 1896 as automobiles became more common and drivers pushed back against the restriction. The modern concept of speed limits tied to road design and safety data only emerged in the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 学校限制学生使用手机。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xiànzhì xuésheng shǐyòng shǒujī.
examples.english: The school restricts students' use of phones.

examples.hanzi: 这个活动对年龄没有限制。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huódòng duì niánlíng méiyǒu xiànzhì.
examples.english: This activity has no age limit.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 找 is to search with the hands. The right part 戈 is not a useful clue.
回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.

example.hanzi: 她终于找回了丢失的钱包。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú zhǎohuí le diūshī de qiánbāo.
example.english: She finally retrieved her lost wallet.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer. It sat corroded on the seafloor for roughly 2,000 years before sponge divers found it. Researchers are still using X-ray imaging today to decode inscriptions on its fragments.

examples.hanzi: 我的猫跑丢了，终于被找回来了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de māo pǎo diū le, zhōngyú bèi zhǎo huílái le.
examples.english: My cat ran off and was finally found again.

examples.hanzi: 他想找回自己的自信。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zhǎohuí zìjǐ de zìxìn.
examples.english: He wants to get his confidence back.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扎 is to bind or prick with the hand.

example.hanzi: 我的手指被针扎了一下。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒuzhǐ bèi zhēn zhā le yíxià.
example.english: My finger got pricked by a needle.
example.fact: 扎 has several readings: zhā is 'to prick' or 'to pitch' (扎营, to camp), zā is 'to tie up' (扎辫子, braid hair), and zhá appears in 挣扎 'to struggle'. Pick the reading by meaning.

examples.hanzi: 他的脚被钉子扎了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiǎo bèi dīngzi zhā le.
examples.english: His foot was pricked by a nail.

examples.hanzi: 我们在湖边扎了一个帐篷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài húbiān zhā le yí ge zhàngpeng.
examples.english: We pitched a tent by the lake.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.

example.hanzi: 这条围巾是手工制的。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo wéijīn shì shǒugōng zhì de.
example.english: This scarf is handmade.
example.fact: Simplified 制 merges two older characters: 制 'to control, a system' (制度) and 製 'to make' (制造). So the same shape covers both meanings now, and context decides which one applies.

examples.hanzi: 这个产品是中国制造的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn shì Zhōngguó zhìzào de.
examples.english: This product is made in China.

examples.hanzi: 请遵守公司的制度。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zūnshǒu gōngsī de zhìdù.
examples.english: Please follow the company's rules.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) with a flag 方: a clan or troop gathered under its banner, with arrows at hand.

example.hanzi: 中国有五十六个民族。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔshíliù gè mínzú.
example.english: China has fifty-six ethnic groups.
example.fact: 族 is the base of 民族 (nationality, ethnic group) and 家族 (family clan). As a modern suffix, it labels groups with shared habits: 上班族 (office workers), 月光族 (people who spend their whole salary each month).

examples.hanzi: 上班族每天都很忙。
examples.pinyin: Shàngbānzú měitiān dōu hěn máng.
examples.english: Office workers are busy every day.

examples.hanzi: 这个家族有很长的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiāzú yǒu hěn cháng de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This family clan has a long history.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 在他的领导之下，公司业绩大幅提升。
example.pinyin: zài tā de lǐngdǎo zhīxià, gōngsī yèjì dàfú tíshēng.
example.english: Under his leadership, the company's performance improved significantly.
example.fact: Roughly 71% of Earth's surface lies under the ocean, yet more than 80% of that underwater world remains unmapped and unexplored in any real detail, according to NOAA. We actually have more detailed maps of the surface of Mars and the Moon than we do of our own ocean floor. The deepest known point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below sea level.

examples.hanzi: 在大家的帮助之下，我完成了任务。
examples.pinyin: Zài dàjiā de bāngzhù zhīxià, wǒ wánchéng le rènwu.
examples.english: With everyone's help, I completed the task.

examples.hanzi: 这只小猫睡在桌子之下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo māo shuì zài zhuōzi zhīxià.
examples.english: The kitten is sleeping under the table.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿; 肮脏 means dirty.
亢 (kàng) is only a loose hint for āng; 抗 kàng and 航 háng share it.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 脏 is an organ (zàng), and also dirty (zāng).
庄 (zhuāng) is a near sound match for zàng/zāng; also in 装 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 街道两旁堆满了肮脏的垃圾。
example.pinyin: jiēdào liǎngpáng duī mǎn le āngzāng de lājī.
example.english: Piles of filthy garbage lined both sides of the street.
example.fact: London's Great Stink of 1858 was so severe — caused by raw sewage flowing directly into the Thames during a summer heatwave — that it reportedly drove Parliament to finally fund a massive new sewer system, designed by engineer Joseph Bazalgette. That system, completed in the 1870s, dramatically reduced outbreaks of cholera in the city and is still partly in use today. Before this, doctors mistakenly believed diseases like cholera spread through foul-smelling air rather than contaminated water.

examples.hanzi: 雨后的街道又湿又肮脏。
examples.pinyin: Yǔ hòu de jiēdào yòu shī yòu āngzāng.
examples.english: After the rain, the street is wet and filthy.

examples.hanzi: 他的手很肮脏，快去洗洗。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒu hěn āngzāng, kuài qù xǐxi.
examples.english: His hands are filthy; go wash them quickly.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 这位大夫在朝廷任职多年。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi dàfū zài cháotíng rènzhí duō nián.
example.english: This senior official has served in the imperial court for many years.
example.fact: In ancient China's Zhou dynasty aristocratic hierarchy, "dàfū" denoted a rank of nobility below feudal lords but above common officials, roughly comparable to a minister or senior court official. Over time, the same characters came to colloquially mean "physician" in modern Mandarin, pronounced with a different tone, reflecting how court physicians once held elevated status. This dual meaning still causes confusion for language learners today.

examples.hanzi: 大夫说我需要多休息。
examples.pinyin: Dàifu shuō wǒ xūyào duō xiūxi.
examples.english: The doctor said I need to rest more.

examples.hanzi: 我生病了，想去看大夫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēngbìng le, xiǎng qù kàn dàifu.
examples.english: I'm sick and want to see a doctor.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 天空中有无数颗星星。
example.pinyin: tiānkōng zhōng yǒu wúshù kē xīngxing.
example.english: There are countless stars in the sky.
example.fact: Astronomers estimate there are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches — roughly 10^24 stars compared to an estimated 10^18 to 10^20 grains of sand. Yet on a clear night without light pollution, the human eye can typically see only about 2,500 to 5,000 individual stars at once. The Milky Way alone is thought to contain 100 to 400 billion stars.

examples.hanzi: 这里有无数的游客。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu wúshù de yóukè.
examples.english: There are countless tourists here.

examples.hanzi: 他为这件事想了无数次。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè jiàn shì xiǎng le wúshù cì.
examples.english: He thought about this matter countless times.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 练 first meant boiling silk to soften it, then practice.
柬 (jiǎn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 炼 liàn and 简 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 演员们正在为演出排练。
example.pinyin: yǎnyuánmen zhèngzài wèi yǎnchū páiliàn.
example.english: The actors are rehearsing for the performance.
example.fact: The Metropolitan Opera in New York typically rehearses a new production for six to eight weeks before opening night, with singers, orchestra, and stagehands coordinating hundreds of technical cues. Maria Callas, one of the most famous opera singers of the 20th century, was known for insisting on exhaustive rehearsals to perfect both her vocal technique and dramatic acting. Even after decades of experience, professional performers rarely skip rehearsal for a new role.

examples.hanzi: 我们明天下午要排练。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān xiàwǔ yào páiliàn.
examples.english: We have to rehearse tomorrow afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 合唱团每周排练两次。
examples.pinyin: Héchàngtuán měi zhōu páiliàn liǎng cì.
examples.english: The choir rehearses twice a week.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 洗, 海; 澡 is bathing.
喿 (zào) — same sound — 澡 is zǎo; 喿 also sounds out 燥 zào and 操 cāo.

example.hanzi: 我每天晚上都洗澡。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang dōu xǐzǎo.
example.english: I take a bath every evening.
example.fact: 澡 is almost never used alone: 洗澡 ('wash bath') is a verb-object phrase, so the verb can split around it — 洗了个澡 'took a bath', not 洗澡了个.

examples.hanzi: 他洗了一个热水澡。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐ le yí ge rèshuǐ zǎo.
examples.english: He took a hot bath.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷喜欢去澡堂。
examples.pinyin: Yéye xǐhuan qù zǎotáng.
examples.english: Grandpa likes going to the bathhouse.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 这篇文章引起了很多评论。
example.pinyin: zhè piān wénzhāng yǐnqǐ le hěn duō pínglùn.
example.english: This article sparked a lot of commentary.
example.fact: The world's first newspaper opinion columns are often traced to 18th-century London publications like The Spectator, founded in 1711 by Joseph Addison and Richard Steele, which used a fictional narrator to comment on daily life and social manners. It ran for only about two years but influenced essay writing and journalism for generations after. Its format — short, witty daily commentary — is considered a direct ancestor of the modern opinion column.

examples.hanzi: 我想评论一下这部电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng pínglùn yíxià zhè bù diànyǐng.
examples.english: I'd like to comment on this movie.

examples.hanzi: 他的评论很有道理。
examples.pinyin: Tā de pínglùn hěn yǒu dàolǐ.
examples.english: His comment makes a lot of sense.

meanings: (idiom) to stand out from the crowd

components.note: The shape does not explain 与 today (simplified from 與, two hands handing something over). Memory aid: a hand passing a thing along, hence 'give' and then 'and, with'.
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 她的穿衣风格总是与众不同。
example.pinyin: tā de chuānyī fēnggé zǒngshì yǔzhòngbùtóng.
example.english: Her style of dress always stands out from the crowd.
example.fact: The axolotl, a salamander native to Mexico's Xochimilco wetlands, stands out among amphibians because it typically never undergoes full metamorphosis, retaining its gills and aquatic juvenile form throughout its adult life, a trait called neoteny. It's also famous for its extraordinary ability to fully regenerate lost limbs, its spinal cord, and even parts of its heart and brain without scarring. Scientists study axolotls closely, hoping to unlock clues for regenerative medicine in humans.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子的想法与众不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi de xiǎngfǎ yǔzhòngbùtóng.
examples.english: This child's ideas are unique.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜与众不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài yǔzhòngbùtóng.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is distinctive.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).
良 (liáng) — good; as a part it sounds out 粮 liáng, 狼 láng, 浪 làng and 朗 lǎng.

example.hanzi: 她心地善良，总是帮助别人。
example.pinyin: tā xīndì shànliáng, zǒngshì bāngzhù biérén.
example.english: She is kindhearted and always helps others.
example.fact: Studies in behavioral science have found that acts of kindness activate the brain's reward circuitry in ways similar to receiving a reward oneself, a phenomenon sometimes called the "helper's high." Research by social psychologists has also shown that witnessing someone else's generosity can inspire onlookers to behave more kindly themselves, an effect known as moral elevation. Some researchers argue this cascading effect helps explain how cooperative behavior spreads through communities.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个善良的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge shànliáng de rén.
examples.english: He's a kind-hearted person.

examples.hanzi: 善良的老奶奶经常喂流浪猫。
examples.pinyin: Shànliáng de lǎo nǎinai jīngcháng wèi liúlàng māo.
examples.english: The kind old lady often feeds stray cats.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke; 烫 is scalding, as in 烫伤 burn or ironing.
汤 (tāng) — close sound: 烫 tàng. 汤 means hot soup.

example.hanzi: 小心，这杯茶很烫。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè bēi chá hěn tàng.
example.english: Careful, this cup of tea is scalding.
example.fact: 烫 is hotter than 热: it means 'hot enough to burn you', as in 烫手. The same character covers 烫头发 (to perm hair) and 烫衣服 (to iron clothes), both involving heat.

examples.hanzi: 这碗汤太烫了,等一会儿再喝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng tài tàng le, děng yíhuìr zài hē.
examples.english: This soup is too hot; wait a bit before drinking.

examples.hanzi: 她把衣服烫平了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yīfu tàng píng le.
examples.english: She ironed the clothes flat.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
心 (heart) — 心 marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 怒; 悲 is sorrow.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 悲 is bēi; 非 also sounds out 辈 bèi and 排 pái.

example.hanzi: 他的处境实在可悲。
example.pinyin: tā de chǔjìng shízài kěbēi.
example.english: His situation is truly lamentable.
example.fact: The dodo, a flightless bird native only to the island of Mauritius, went extinct within roughly a century of European sailors arriving in the late 16th century, done in by hunting, introduced predators, and habitat destruction. It became one of the most cited symbols of human-caused extinction, giving rise to the phrase "dead as a dodo." No complete skeleton of a dodo survives today; scientific reconstructions rely on scattered bones and a handful of contemporary illustrations.

examples.hanzi: 这种结果太可悲了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiéguǒ tài kěbēi le.
examples.english: This result is truly pitiful.

examples.hanzi: 他觉得自己可悲又无助。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ kěbēi yòu wúzhù.
examples.english: He feels pitiful and helpless.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.hanzi: 图书馆里不准大声说话。
example.pinyin: túshūguǎn lǐ bùzhǔn dàshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: Loud talking is not allowed in the library.
example.fact: Venice has banned large cruise ships from its historic lagoon since 2021, after years of concern that the massive vessels were eroding the foundations of the centuries-old city and disturbing its fragile ecosystem. The city had already been listed by UNESCO as at risk partly due to the strain from mass tourism. Cruise passengers must now dock at a more distant industrial port and transfer into the city by other means.

examples.hanzi: 这里不准抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù zhǔn chōuyān.
examples.english: Smoking is not allowed here.

examples.hanzi: 老师不准我们迟到。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bù zhǔn wǒmen chídào.
examples.english: The teacher doesn't allow us to be late.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 这家公司管理着一个大型投资基金。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī guǎnlǐzhe yí gè dàxíng tóuzī jījīn.
example.english: This company manages a large investment fund.
example.fact: The Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global, often called simply "the Oil Fund," is one of the largest sovereign wealth funds in the world, holding over $1.4 trillion in assets built from the country's oil and gas revenue since 1996. It owns small stakes in thousands of companies across nearly every country on Earth, and by some estimates owns roughly 1.5% of all publicly listed companies worldwide. The fund is managed under strict ethical investment guidelines that have led it to divest from companies involved in coal, tobacco, and certain weapons manufacturing.

examples.hanzi: 他把钱存进了一个教育基金。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qián cún jìn le yí ge jiàoyù jījīn.
examples.english: He put the money into an education fund.

examples.hanzi: 这个基金会帮助贫困学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jījīnhuì bāngzhù pínkùn xuésheng.
examples.english: This foundation helps students in need.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 这支球队赢得了全国冠军。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì yíngdé le quánguó guànjūn.
example.english: This team won the national championship.
example.fact: The English football club Sheffield FC, founded in 1857, is recognized by FIFA as the oldest association football club in the world still in existence today. It predates the founding of the English Football Association itself by six years, and some of its early rules directly influenced the sport's modern laws. The club still plays in England's lower non-league divisions.

examples.hanzi: 我们球队下周有比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qiúduì xià zhōu yǒu bǐsài.
examples.english: Our team has a game next week.

examples.hanzi: 他是这支球队的队长。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhè zhī qiúduì de duìzhǎng.
examples.english: He is the captain of this team.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and relations, as in 说, 请, 议; 谊 is friendship.
宜 (yí) hints at the sound: 谊 yì is close, and 宜 also means fitting.

example.hanzi: 他们之间的友谊持续了三十年。
example.pinyin: tāmen zhījiān de yǒuyì chíxù le sānshí nián.
example.english: Their friendship has lasted thirty years.
example.fact: Harvard's Study of Adult Development, which has tracked participants for over 80 years since 1938, found that the quality of a person's close relationships, including friendships, is one of the strongest predictors of happiness and even physical health in old age — a stronger predictor than wealth, fame, or IQ. The study is one of the longest-running research projects on human life ever conducted. Its lead researchers have continued publishing findings well into the 21st century.

examples.hanzi: 我们的友谊很深。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de yǒuyì hěn shēn.
examples.english: Our friendship is deep.

examples.hanzi: 为了友谊，干杯！
examples.pinyin: Wèile yǒuyì, gānbēi!
examples.english: To friendship, cheers!

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 侧 is the side or lean, as in 侧面.
则 (zé) — close sound: 侧 cè. 则 also sounds out 测 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 请从左侧通过。
example.pinyin: Qǐng cóng zuǒ cè tōngguò.
example.english: Please pass on the left side.
example.fact: 侧 means a side or flank, in compounds like 侧面 (profile, side view), 左侧 / 右侧 and 侧身 (to turn sideways). It is a little more formal than 边.

examples.hanzi: 他侧着身子走了过去。
examples.pinyin: Tā cè zhe shēnzi zǒu le guòqù.
examples.english: He walked past sideways.

examples.hanzi: 房子的右侧有一个小花园。
examples.pinyin: Fángzi de yòucè yǒu yí ge xiǎo huāyuán.
examples.english: There is a small garden on the right side of the house.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 下雨了，我们还是别出门了。
example.pinyin: xiàyǔ le, wǒmen háishì bié chūmén le.
example.english: It's raining, let's not go out.
example.fact: The invention of the umbrella dates back over 3,000 years, with early depictions found in ancient Egyptian, Assyrian, and Chinese art, though these early versions were primarily used as sunshades for royalty rather than rain protection. Waterproofing umbrellas for rain became common much later, and the folding umbrella wasn't widely popularized in the West until the 18th century. Jonas Hanway, an English philanthropist, is often credited with popularizing rain umbrellas for men in London around 1750, despite public ridicule at the time.

examples.hanzi: 今天太冷了，我不想出门。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tài lěng le, wǒ bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.english: It's too cold today; I don't want to go out.

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上八点出门上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang bā diǎn chūmén shàngbān.
examples.english: He leaves home for work at eight every morning.

components.note: 食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.

example.hanzi: 我们一起去吃晚餐吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù chī wǎncān ba.
example.english: Let's go have dinner together.
example.fact: 餐 is the measure word of meals: 一日三餐 (three meals a day). It sounds more formal than 饭, as in 早餐 (breakfast), 西餐 (Western food) and 用餐 ('to dine'), and 餐厅 is a restaurant or dining hall.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的早餐很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de zǎocān hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: The breakfast at this restaurant is very rich.

examples.hanzi: 我们点了两份套餐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diǎn le liǎng fèn tàocān.
examples.english: We ordered two set meals.

components.note: 王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.
八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.

example.hanzi: 河里游着一只王八。
example.pinyin: hé lǐ yóuzhe yì zhī wángba.
example.english: A softshell turtle is swimming in the river.
example.fact: The Chinese softshell turtle can absorb oxygen directly through specialized skin structures in its throat and cloaca, allowing it to stay submerged in water for extended periods without surfacing to breathe air. This adaptation, called cloacal respiration, is also seen in some other freshwater turtle species. Softshell turtles are farmed extensively in parts of East Asia both for food and traditional medicine markets.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷在池塘边看到一只王八。
examples.pinyin: Yéye zài chítáng biān kàn dào yì zhī wángba.
examples.english: Grandpa saw a turtle by the pond.

examples.hanzi: 这只王八爬得很慢。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī wángba pá de hěn màn.
examples.english: This turtle crawls very slowly.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 全国代表大会将在北京召开。
example.pinyin: quánguó dàibiǎo dàhuì jiāng zài Běijīng zhàokāi.
example.english: The National People's Congress will convene in Beijing.
example.fact: The United Nations General Assembly, first convened in London in January 1946, now brings together representatives from 193 member states annually in New York to debate global issues ranging from climate change to international security. Its General Debate each September regularly causes the biggest security and traffic disruption of the year in Manhattan. Each member state, regardless of size or population, gets exactly one vote in the Assembly.

examples.hanzi: 明天上午有一个大会。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ yǒu yí ge dàhuì.
examples.english: There is a general meeting tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 大会在体育馆举行。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuì zài tǐyùguǎn jǔxíng.
examples.english: The assembly is held in the gymnasium.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 请帮我占一个位子,谢谢。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ zhàn yī gè wèizi, xièxie.
example.english: Please save a seat for me, thanks.
example.fact: Airplane economy seats have actually shrunk over time: standard seat width has dropped from about 18.5 inches in the 1980s to as little as 16.5 inches today, even as average passenger body size increased over the same period. Airlines made the tradeoff to fit more rows into the same fuselage length.

examples.hanzi: 电影院里还有几个空位子。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐngyuàn lǐ hái yǒu jǐ ge kòng wèizi.
examples.english: There are still a few empty seats in the cinema.

examples.hanzi: 你坐这个位子吧，我坐那边。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò zhège wèizi ba, wǒ zuò nàbiān.
examples.english: You take this seat, and I'll sit over there.

meanings: not having learned to do sth

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 别担心,我不会告诉别人的。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ bùhuì gàosù biérén de.
example.english: Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
example.fact: Research by psychologist Michael Slepian found that people think about the secrets they're keeping roughly once a day on average, and that it's the mental burden of concealment itself — not the topic of the secret — that makes carrying one feel exhausting.

examples.hanzi: 今天太晚了，他不会来了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tài wǎn le, tā bú huì lái le.
examples.english: It is too late today, so he won't be coming.

examples.hanzi: 他不会开车，每天坐地铁。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú huì kāichē, měitiān zuò dìtiě.
examples.english: He can't drive, so he takes the subway every day.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 下一位选手准备上场了。
example.pinyin: Xià yī wèi xuǎnshǒu zhǔnbèi shàngchǎng le.
example.english: The next contestant is getting ready to go on stage.
example.fact: Glossophobia, the fear of public speaking, affects a large majority of people to some degree, and it triggers the same fight-or-flight surge of adrenaline that the body uses when facing a physical threat — the nervous system doesn't distinguish a stage from a predator.

examples.hanzi: 球员们已经在场边准备上场了。
examples.pinyin: Qiúyuánmen yǐjīng zài chǎng biān zhǔnbèi shàngchǎng le.
examples.english: The players are already ready to go on the field.

examples.hanzi: 他受伤了，不能上场比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, bù néng shàngchǎng bǐsài.
examples.english: He's injured and can't play in the game.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes, as in 阶 steps, 院, 陆; 降 is to go down a slope.
夅 (two feet going down) — shows descent, and gives the sound: 降 jiàng.

example.hanzi: 敌军最终选择了投降。
example.pinyin: Díjūn zuìzhōng xuǎnzéle tóuxiáng.
example.english: The enemy army ultimately chose to surrender.
example.fact: Japan's formal World War II surrender took place aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945. The signing ceremony that ended a six-year global war lasted only about 23 minutes.

examples.hanzi: 他们被包围了，只好投降。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bèi bāowéi le, zhǐhǎo tóuxiáng.
examples.english: They were surrounded and had to surrender.

examples.hanzi: 我宁愿努力到底，也不会投降。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nìngyuàn nǔlì dàodǐ, yě bú huì tóuxiáng.
examples.english: I'd rather work hard to the end than give up.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 湖的表面在阳光下闪闪发光。
example.pinyin: Hú de biǎomiàn zài yángguāng xià shǎnshǎn fāguāng.
example.english: The surface of the lake sparkles in the sunlight.
example.fact: Water's surface tension is strong enough that insects like the water strider can walk across it without breaking through, spreading their weight over thousands of tiny water-repelling hairs on each leg.

examples.hanzi: 桌子的表面很光滑。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi de biǎomiàn hěn guānghuá.
examples.english: The surface of the table is very smooth.

examples.hanzi: 别只看表面，要了解真实情况。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhǐ kàn biǎomiàn, yào liǎojiě zhēnshí qíngkuàng.
examples.english: Don't just look at the surface; find out the real situation.

components.note: 凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 那支箭正好击中了目标的中心。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī jiàn zhènghǎo jīzhòngle mùbiāo de zhōngxīn.
example.english: That arrow hit right in the center of the target.
example.fact: In Olympic target archery, athletes shoot from 70 meters away at a target face whose center ring is only about 12 centimeters wide — meaning a fraction of a degree of aiming error is the difference between a perfect score and a total miss.

examples.hanzi: 他投出的球击中了窗户。
examples.pinyin: Tā tóu chū de qiú jīzhòng le chuānghu.
examples.english: The ball he threw hit the window.

examples.hanzi: 子弹没有击中目标。
examples.pinyin: Zǐdàn méiyǒu jīzhòng mùbiāo.
examples.english: The bullet didn't hit the target.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.

example.hanzi: 球迷们为进球欢呼起来。
example.pinyin: Qiúmímen wèi jìnqiú huānhū qǐlái.
example.english: The fans cheered for the goal.
example.fact: The loudest crowd roar ever recorded at a sports stadium reached 142.2 decibels, set by Kansas City Chiefs fans in 2014 — louder than a jet engine at takeoff, and loud enough to risk hearing damage with prolonged exposure.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们看到雪都欢呼起来。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen kàn dào xuě dōu huānhū qǐlai.
examples.english: The children all cheered when they saw the snow.

examples.hanzi: 观众为歌手热烈欢呼。
examples.pinyin: Guānzhòng wèi gēshǒu rèliè huānhū.
examples.english: The audience cheered enthusiastically for the singer.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and coverings, as in 布, 帽, 带, 帮; 席 is a woven mat, then a seat or place at a table.

example.hanzi: 他被选为公司的新任主席。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi gōngsī de xīnrèn zhǔxí.
example.english: He was elected the company's new chairperson.
example.fact: Separating the chairperson and CEO roles into two different people is now standard governance practice at more than half of S&P 500 companies, up from roughly a fifth of them two decades earlier, as boards sought clearer checks on executive power.

examples.hanzi: 学生会主席明天要讲话。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshēnghuì zhǔxí míngtiān yào jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The student union chairman will give a speech tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 主席请大家安静。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔxí qǐng dàjiā ānjìng.
examples.english: The chairperson asked everyone to be quiet.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.
石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.

example.hanzi: 这个天气预报相当准确。
example.pinyin: Zhège tiānqì yùbào xiāngdāng zhǔnquè.
example.english: This weather forecast is quite accurate.
example.fact: One-day weather forecasts are correct roughly 90% of the time, but accuracy drops sharply after about a week, because the atmosphere behaves as a chaotic system where tiny measurement errors roughly double every few days — the origin of the popular 'butterfly effect' idea.

examples.hanzi: 请准确地告诉我你的地址。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhǔnquè de gàosu wǒ nǐ de dìzhǐ.
examples.english: Please tell me your address accurately.

examples.hanzi: 这个数字不太准确。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shùzì bú tài zhǔnquè.
examples.english: This number is not very accurate.

components.note: 知 (zhī, know) — gives the sound (zhì is close) and the idea: knowing well is wisdom, as in 智慧.
心 (heart, mind) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 慧 is a bright mind.
彗 (huì) gives the sound exactly: 慧 huì.

example.hanzi: 老人的智慧来自多年的生活经验。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén de zhìhuì láizì duōnián de shēnghuó jīngyàn.
example.english: The old man's wisdom comes from years of life experience.
example.fact: Aging research shows that while raw processing speed tends to decline with age, 'crystallized intelligence' — accumulated knowledge and judgment — keeps growing well into a person's sixties and seventies, which is part of why wisdom-related skills often peak later in life.

examples.hanzi: 读书能给人带来智慧。
examples.pinyin: Dúshū néng gěi rén dàilái zhìhuì.
examples.english: Reading can bring people wisdom.

examples.hanzi: 他用智慧解决了这个难题。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng zhìhuì jiějué le zhège nántí.
examples.english: He solved this difficult problem with wisdom.

components.note: 足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.

example.hanzi: 钱已经足够了。
example.pinyin: Qián yǐjīng zúgòu le.
example.english: The money is already enough.
example.fact: 足 is the written word for 'foot' (spoken Chinese says 脚), and it is the root of 足球 (football). It also means 'enough', as in 足够 and 充足, and is the radical in many foot-related characters.

examples.hanzi: 他每天睡足八个小时。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān shuì zú bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: He gets a full eight hours of sleep every day.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在操场上踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài cāochǎng shang tī zúqiú.
examples.english: The kids are playing soccer on the field.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the bottom part, as in 灯 lamp and 炎 flame. The dictionary lists fire as the hint: a spirit like a flickering flame, as in 灵魂.
彐 (snout) — the top part, a stroke group as in 当 and 归. 灵 simplifies 靈, so this shape is not a sound clue. Memory aid: a hand over a flame, feeling a spirit.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 这幅画的灵感来自一次日出。
example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de línggǎn láizì yī cì rìchū.
example.english: This painting's inspiration came from a sunrise.
example.fact: Sunrises look reddish-orange because sunlight passing through more atmosphere at a low angle scatters away shorter blue wavelengths, a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, leaving mostly the longer red and orange wavelengths to reach the eye.

examples.hanzi: 我最近没有灵感，写不出歌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn méiyǒu línggǎn, xiě bu chū gē.
examples.english: I have no inspiration lately and can't write songs.

examples.hanzi: 散步的时候，他突然有了灵感。
examples.pinyin: Sànbù de shíhou, tā tūrán yǒu le línggǎn.
examples.english: While taking a walk, he suddenly got an inspiration.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 海, 河, 湖; 漫 is water overflowing, then spreading freely.
曼 (màn) — same sound — 漫 is màn; 曼 also sounds out 慢 màn.
田 (field) — 画 (simplified 畫) originally showed a brush 聿 drawing the borders of a field: to draw lines, hence a picture.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢看漫画。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan kàn mànhuà.
example.english: He has loved reading comics since he was little.
example.fact: At its 1995 peak, the Japanese manga magazine Weekly Shonen Jump sold over 6 million copies per issue — more circulation in a single week than most countries' entire national magazine markets combined.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟每周都买新漫画。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi měi zhōu dōu mǎi xīn mànhuà.
examples.english: My younger brother buys new comics every week.

examples.hanzi: 这本漫画书很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn mànhuà shū hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This comic book is very interesting.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses, as in 花, 草, 茶; 莎 is a sedge grass, seen in 莎士比亚 Shakespeare.
沙 (shā) gives the sound: 莎 shā, also in 纱 shā and 鲨 shā.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.

example.hanzi: 莎拉每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: Shālā měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: Sarah goes jogging every morning.
example.fact: The long-running Copenhagen City Heart Study linked regular light-to-moderate jogging to several added years of life expectancy compared with being sedentary, with the biggest benefit found at just one to two and a half hours of jogging per week — more wasn't necessarily better.

examples.hanzi: 莎拉是我的英语老师。
examples.pinyin: Shālā shì wǒ de Yīngyǔ lǎoshī.
examples.english: Sarah is my English teacher.

examples.hanzi: 莎拉打算下个月去中国旅游。
examples.pinyin: Shālā dǎsuàn xià ge yuè qù Zhōngguó lǚyóu.
examples.english: Sarah plans to travel to China next month.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.

example.hanzi: 这本书探讨了亲密关系中的性爱话题。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū tàntǎole qīnmì guānxì zhōng de xìng'ài huàtí.
example.english: This book explores the topic of intimacy in close relationships.
example.fact: The hormone oxytocin, often called the 'bonding hormone,' is released during both physical intimacy and childbirth, and studies have measured its role in promoting trust and social bonding between the people who experience its release together.

examples.hanzi: 学校的健康课会讲到性爱知识。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào de jiànkāng kè huì jiǎng dào xìng'ài zhīshi.
examples.english: The school's health class covers sex education.

examples.hanzi: 医生建议他们公开讨论性爱问题。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tāmen gōngkāi tǎolùn xìng'ài wèntí.
examples.english: The doctor advised them to discuss intimacy issues openly.
